defs.def: belonging to sb; relating to sb 属于（某人）；关于（某人）

ex.s: SoFi Stadium is the go-to destination in the heart of Los Angeles for sports fans.
ex.t: SoFi体育场位于洛杉矶市中心，是体育迷们的首选目的地。

ex.s: Each parking zone consists of multiple lots, designed to efficiently manage traffic across the venue’s network.
ex.t: 每个停车区由多个停车场组成，旨在高效管理整个场馆范围内的交通。

ex.s: Not long ago, my fifth-grade son Kevin asked me about the meaning of a word in a novel.
ex.t: 不久前，我上五年级的儿子凯文问我一本小说里一个词的意思。

ex.s: I took down one of the dictionaries, and we read it together for a few minutes before I handed it to him.
ex.t: 我取下一本词典，和他一起读了几分钟，然后把它交给了他。

ex.s: “But that’s why this is one of my favorite books.”
ex.t: “但这正是它成为我最喜欢的书之一的原因。”

ex.s: I felt a small pain in my chest The dictionary was stolen at the end of my freshman year of college.
ex.t: 我胸口隐隐作痛——那本词典在我大一结束时被偷了。

ex.s: I still made it through the next three years of college, even without the book.
ex.t: 即使没有那本书，我也顺利读完了大学剩下的三年。

ex.s: What does Kevin usually do to get the meaning of a word?
ex.t: 凯文通常用什么方法来了解一个词的意思？

ex.s: In line with longstanding initiatives to expand its green spaces, New York City is planting tens of thousands of trees each year.
ex.t: 为配合长期以来扩大绿色空间的举措，纽约市每年种植数万棵树木。

ex.s: They provide shade, lower surface temperatures, absorb a surprising amount of airborne carbon, remove tiny pollutants, and provide wildlife habitat along with just plain beauty.
ex.t: 它们提供树荫、降低地表温度、吸收空气中惊人数量的碳、去除微小污染物，还为野生动物提供栖息地，并带来纯粹的美感。

ex.s: Oaks and sweetgums, which currently account for a majority of the city’s trees, produce huge amounts of a chemical substance called isoprene.
ex.t: 橡树和枫香树目前占纽约市树木的大多数，它们会产生大量一种叫作异戊二烯的化学物质。

ex.s: A study carried out by some of its researchers several years ago concluded that city trees did release isoprene.
ex.t: 该局一些研究人员几年前开展的一项研究得出结论：城市树木确实会释放异戊二烯。

ex.s: “We didn’t make a big deal of that,” said Novem Auyeung, a Parks Department senior scientist.
ex.t: “我们当时没有把这事看得太重，”公园管理局资深科学家Novem Auyeung说。

ex.s: They affect the growth of other trees.
ex.t: 它们影响其他树木的生长。

ex.s: Which of the following may Commane suggest based on their study?
ex.t: 基于他们的研究，Commane可能会提出以下哪项建议？

ex.s: Changing the species of trees in new plantings.
ex.t: 更换新种植树木的树种。

ex.s: In the study, 187 people were invited to visit Kettle’s Yard gallery during an exhibition of handmade clay objects.
ex.t: 在这项研究中，187人受邀在手工陶艺品展览期间参观了Kettle's Yard美术馆。

ex.s: Participants were randomly divided into two groups: the “beauty” group was asked to actively consider and then rate the beauty of each object they viewed, while the control group just matched a line drawing of the object with the artwork itself.
ex.t: 参与者被随机分成两组：“美感”组被要求主动思考并评价每件所见物品的美，而对照组只是把物品的线描图与艺术品本身进行匹配。

ex.s: Emotional states of participants were also measured by asking about their feelings while completing the gallery task.
ex.t: 研究人员还通过询问参与者完成美术馆任务时的感受，测量了他们的情绪状态。

ex.s: Across all participants, those in the beauty group reported an average of 23% higher levels of “transformative and self-transcendent feelings” — such as feeling moved, enlightened and inspired — than the control group.
ex.t: 在所有参与者中，美感组报告的“蜕变性和超越自我的感受”——如感动、受启迪、受鼓舞——平均比对照组高出23%。

ex.s: “We usually think in very concrete terms when doing something on a screen,” said Simone Schnall, senior author of the study.
ex.t: “我们在屏幕上做事时，通常以非常具体的方式思考，”该研究的资深作者Simone Schnall说。

ex.s: Admiring the beauty of art may be the ideal way to initiate the abstract cognitive processes.”
ex.t: 欣赏艺术之美或许是启动抽象认知过程的理想方式。”

ex.s: Make a copy of each piece.
ex.t: 复制每件作品。

ex.s: To examine the difficulty of the tasks.
ex.t: 为了检验任务的难度。

ex.s: What is the major finding of the study regarding the appreciation of art?
ex.t: 关于艺术欣赏，这项研究的主要发现是什么？

ex.s: Museums, once quiet places filled with history, are now full of digital excitement.
ex.t: 博物馆曾经是充满历史气息的安静场所，如今却处处洋溢着数字化的活力。

ex.s: AI can help identify the slightest signs of decay, such as cracks or discoloration, which are often invisible to the human eye. _____38_____ Moreover, by predicting future decay patterns, AI helps museums take preventive measures and improve preservation strategies.
ex.t: 人工智能可以帮助识别最轻微的损坏迹象，如裂纹或变色，这些往往肉眼难以察觉。____ 此外，通过预测未来的损坏趋势，人工智能帮助博物馆采取预防措施、改进保护策略。

ex.s: AI also significantly enhances the educational value of museums, particularly for children and families. _____39_____ For instance, interactive exhibits powered by AI can adjust their content and difficulty level based on the user's preferences and responses.
ex.t: 人工智能还显著提升了博物馆的教育价值，对儿童和家庭尤其如此。____ 例如，由人工智能驱动的互动展品可以根据用户的偏好和反应调整内容和难度。

ex.s: The _____41_____ of how little people knew about Ohio came quickly after I went to school in central Pennsylvania.
ex.t: 人们对俄亥俄知之甚少，这种____在我到宾夕法尼亚州中部上学后很快就出现了。

ex.s: Though I lived _____42_____ three and a half hours away, most of my classmates thought of Ohio as a whole different world.
ex.t: 尽管我住的地方____只有三个半小时的车程，但大多数同学都觉得俄亥俄完全像是另一个世界。

ex.s: Sure, my friends and I loved to _____46_____ about how bored we were in the middle of nowhere; _____47_____ , as I finish up my junior year of college, I’m convinced that it took _____48_____ our small town to realize how much we actually loved it and what exactly we loved about it.
ex.t: 当然，我和朋友们过去总爱____，抱怨我们在这偏僻地方有多无聊；____，当我大学三年级即将结束时，我确信，正是____我们的小镇，才让我们意识到自己其实有多爱它，以及我们究竟爱它什么。

ex.s: The pace of life is slow and people _____49_____ connecting to each other.
ex.t: 那里的生活节奏缓慢，人们____彼此之间的联系。

ex.s: You do more than just talk to your neighbors — in a lot of cases, they’re truly an _____50_____ of your family.
ex.t: 你不仅仅是和邻居说说话——在很多情况下，他们真的是你家庭的一种____。

ex.s: Much of this
ex.t: 这其中的大部分

ex.t: 人们一边吃吃喝喝、欣赏街头表演，一边相互聊天，分享日常生活的故事。

ex.s: Emily Sanders, a 25-year-old from Detroit, Michigan, set out on December 23rd with high hopes of reaching Toronto to meet her boyfriend for Christmas.
ex.t: 25岁的Emily Sanders来自密歇根州底特律，12月23日她满怀希望地出发，打算赶到多伦多与男友共度圣诞节。

ex.s: While Emily was driving on a narrow stretch of road, her car slid into a ditch (沟).
ex.t: 当Emily行驶在一段狭窄的路上时，她的车滑进了沟里。

ex.s: Seeing no hope of immediate rescue, Emily decided to spend the night in her car.
ex.t: 眼看没有立即获救的希望，Emily决定在车里过夜。

ex.s: It also serves a variety of chef’s specials, beef with rice cakes, and more.
ex.t: 它还供应各种主厨特荐菜、牛肉炒年糕等。

ex.s: The spacious dining room is regularly filled with customers enjoying dumplings and a variety of noodle and rice dishes.
ex.t: 宽敞的餐厅里常常坐满了享用饺子以及各种面条、米饭菜肴的顾客。

ex.s: The house where Reisley has lived for 73 years is located in the woods of Westchester County, New York, just 30 miles north of Manhattan.
ex.t: Reisley住了73年的房子位于纽约州韦斯特切斯特县的树林里，距曼哈顿以北仅30英里。

ex.s: It’s one of 47 that make up the peaceful mid-20th-century modern village of Usonia.
ex.t: 它是组成Usonia这座宁静的20世纪中期现代风格村庄的47座住宅之一。

ex.s: The house is now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
ex.t: 这座房子如今已被列入《国家史迹名录》。

ex.s: He co-founded the Frank Lloyd Wright Building Conservancy, an organization engaged in the preservation of all of Wright’s remaining buildings.
ex.t: 他联合创立了弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特建筑保护协会，该组织致力于保护赖特现存的所有建筑。

ex.s: Reisley believes that his devotion to the home and the community are what have kept him in such good health all of these years.
ex.t: Reisley相信，正是对这座房子和这片社区的热爱，让他多年来一直保持着如此好的健康状态。

ex.s: The convenience of its location.
ex.t: 那里位置的便利。

ex.s: The warmth of its residents.
ex.t: 那里居民的热情。

ex.s: The peak of Mount Qomolangma, 8,849 meters above sea level.
ex.t: 珠穆朗玛峰峰顶，海拔8849米。

ex.s: Chimborazo, 6,263 m; Mont Blanc, 4,806 m; Pradidali hut, at the foot of the Pala group in the Dolomites, 2,278 m.
ex.t: 钦博拉索山，6263米；勃朗峰，4806米；Pradidali小屋，位于多洛米蒂山脉Pala山群脚下，海拔2278米。

ex.s: But elevation is necessarily relative: only the choice of a reference point allows us to express numerically the height of an object or a location.
ex.t: 但海拔必然是相对的：只有选定一个参照点，我们才能用数字表示一个物体或地点的高度。

ex.s: The idea of sea level as a reference point for elevations has by now been around for so long as to go essentially unnoticed-we mention it without even considering what it means.
ex.t: 以海平面作为海拔参照点的想法由来已久，以至于人们基本不再留意——我们提到它时甚至不会去想它意味着什么。

ex.s: We tend to forget that sea level is a product of technically and culturally determined assumptions.
ex.t: 我们往往忘记，海平面其实是由技术和文化因素决定的一系列假设的产物。

ex.s: In this book, I tell a story of these assumptions.
ex.t: 在本书中，我将讲述这些假设的故事。

ex.s: A month after visiting the French Riviera and enjoying the sandy beaches of Nice and Menton, I went hiking with friends in the Pala group.
ex.t: 在游览法国里维埃拉、享受尼斯和芒通的沙滩一个月后，我和朋友们去了Pala山群徒步。

ex.s: This sense of uncertainty led me to think about the meaning of zero.
ex.t: 这种不确定感让我开始思考“零”的意义。

ex.s: This is how I began my search for the conceptual history of sea level.
ex.t: 我就是这样开始探寻海平面的概念史的。

ex.s: In this book I examine three crucial stages in the history of mean sea level.
ex.t: 在本书中，我考察了平均海平面历史上的三个关键阶段。

ex.s: These stages mirror the development of human conceptions of the sea.
ex.t: 这些阶段反映了人类对海洋认知的发展。

ex.s: What does the author point out at the beginning of the text?
ex.t: 作者在文章开头指出了什么？

ex.s: The concept of elevation is relative.
ex.t: 海拔的概念是相对的。

ex.s: What can be the title of the book mentioned in the text?
ex.t: 文中提到的那本书可以取什么书名？

ex.s: Meaning of Zero: Nothing or EverythingD.
ex.t: 《零的意义：虚无还是一切》D.

ex.s: Little do they know that as they do so, a burst of energy is sent up to street level to help charge an electric car.
ex.t: 他们不知道的是，就在此时，一股能量被送上街面，用来为一辆电动汽车充电。

ex.s: “I am pleasantly surprised, because I am always looking for where to plug it in,” Espinoza said before catching the subway in a working-class area of southern Barcelona.
ex.t: “我感到惊喜，因为我总是在找哪里能给它充电，”Espinoza在巴塞罗那南部一个工薪阶层社区乘地铁前说。

ex.s: They consist of an electric motor which collects energy used in the braking action that would be lost as heat by conventional brakes.
ex.t: 它由一个电动机组成，可以收集制动过程中产生的能量——这些能量若用传统制动器则会以热量形式散失。

ex.s: Alvaro Luna, a professor of electrical engineering, said that the system is innovative in so far as it allows for recycled energy to be redirected to specific local uses — in this case powering electric cars parked nearby.
ex.t: 电气工程教授Alvaro Luna表示，该系统的创新之处在于，它能把回收的能量重新导向特定的本地用途——在这个案例中就是为停放在附近的电动汽车供电。

ex.s: To raise the quality of electric cars.
ex.t: 为了提高电动汽车的质量。

ex.s: What aspect of regenerative brakes is discussed in paragraph 5?
ex.t: 第五段讨论了再生制动的哪个方面？

ex.s: It prioritizes the safety of trains.
ex.t: 它把列车安全放在首位。

ex.s: Ever watched your child try to get out of doing housework by making excuses?
ex.t: 有没有见过你的孩子找借口逃避做家务？

ex.s: Few things strike fear into a child’s heart like the prospect of failing.
ex.t: 没什么比害怕失败更让孩子心生恐惧了。

ex.s: Not every child is born with the willpower of a marathon runner.
ex.t: 不是每个孩子天生都有马拉松运动员那样的意志力。

ex.s: And then, at the end of the lesson, one child asked me a question: “Have you always wanted to be a ____46____, Miss?” I explained that when I was his age, I actually wanted to be a writer, but I didn’t think I quite had what it ____47____.
ex.t: 下课时，一个孩子问了我一个问题：“老师，您一直想当____吗？”我解释说，我在他那个年纪时其实想当作家，但我觉得自己不具备那所需要的____。

ex.s: On the basis of that ____53____, I applied to go back to university and study creative writing.
ex.t: 正是基于那次____，我申请重返大学学习创意写作。

ex.s: There were times when I found myself wondering if I should pack it all in, but the boy’s words kept ringing in my ears: I knew I needed nothing else to succeed but a bit of ____54____ and hard work.
ex.t: 有几次我想过要不要干脆放弃，但男孩的话一直在我耳边回响：我知道，成功所需要的不过是一点____和勤奋。

ex.s: I ____55____ to find a way out of my shame and into a pattern of work that I loved.
ex.t: 我____走出羞愧，找到了自己热爱的工作模式。

ex.s: Angela, a tai chi ____57____ (instruct) with twenty-eight years of experience, says that a successful hour of tai chi is an hour with no negative thoughts.
ex.t: Angela是一位有28年经验的太极拳____（教练），她说，成功的一小时太极，就是没有任何消极念头的一小时。

ex.s: We move on to tai chi positions, of ____61____ there are forty-two in the style that Angela teaches.
ex.t: 接着我们练习太极招式，Angela所教的这一流派共有____四十二式。

ex.s: At the end of the lesson, I feel wide awake, despite it still ____64____ (be) early at 8 am.
ex.t: 课程结束时，尽管才早上8点、仍然____（是）很早，我却感觉神清气爽。

ex.s: It’s a great idea to make a collection of our English essays.
ex.t: 把我们的英语作文汇集成册是个好主意。

ex.s: I found comfort in keeping myself awake when everyone else had gone to bed, and I loved the silence of the night.
ex.t: 当其他人都睡了，我却在清醒中感到慰藉，我喜爱夜晚的宁静。

ex.s: My parents urged me to get out of this so-called unhealthy habit, but their repeated requests fell on deaf ears.
ex.t: 父母劝我改掉这个所谓不健康的习惯，但他们的一再要求都被我当成了耳旁风。

ex.s: Fast forward to my first year of college.
ex.t: 快进到我大学一年级。

ex.s: Bent over my laptop while sitting on the bed in the corner of my room, I suddenly felt a pounding headache, and had to lie down.
ex.t: 我弓着背坐在房间角落的床上盯着笔记本电脑，突然感到一阵剧烈的头痛，不得不躺下。

ex.t: 当我让他们看到我校外生活的一面时，一些同样喜欢汽车的学生与我更亲近了，也更投入我的课程。

ex.s: Human beings have always loved reviews: word of mouth has long been regarded as one of the most valuable marketing tools available to a company.
ex.t: 人类向来喜欢评价：口碑长期以来一直被视为公司最有价值的营销工具之一。

ex.s: Shabnam Azimi and Alexander Krasnikov of Loyola University of Chicago and Kwong Chan of Northeastern University recently published a study on fake reviews.
ex.t: 芝加哥洛约拉大学的Shabnam Azimi和Alexander Krasnikov以及东北大学的Kwong Chan最近发表了一项关于虚假评论的研究。

ex.s: The study used a dataset of 1,600 reviews of Chicago hotels.
ex.t: 该研究使用了一个包含1600条芝加哥酒店评论的数据集。

ex.s: Some of them were real; others were fake.
ex.t: 其中一些是真实的，另一些是虚假的。

ex.s: Each subject got eight reviews to read: a balanced set of two positive fake, two positive real, two negative fake and two negative real, presented in a random order.
ex.t: 每名受试者读到8条评论：两条正面虚假、两条正面真实、两条负面虚假、两条负面真实，均衡搭配并随机排序。

ex.s: A long, negative review of a hotel, complete with lots of information, tended to convince participants.
ex.t: 一条内容翔实的长篇酒店负面评论往往能取信于参与者。

ex.s: Emotion was also important in convincing readers — or the lack of emotion, at least.
ex.t: 情感表达对于说服读者也很重要——或者说，情感的缺失至少同样重要。

ex.s: When reading texts of several hundred words or more, learning is generally more successful when it’s on paper than onscreen.
ex.t: 阅读几百词或更长的文本时，在纸上学习通常比在屏幕上更成功。

ex.s: A large amount of research confirms this finding.
ex.t: 大量研究证实了这一发现。

ex.s: The benefits of print reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from posing simple tasks — like identifying the main idea in a reading passage — to ones that require mental abstraction — such as drawing inferences from a text.
ex.t: 当实验者从布置简单任务（如找出阅读段落的主旨）转向需要抽象思维的任务（如从文本中推断结论）时，纸质阅读的优势就格外明显地显现出来。

ex.s: With paper, there is a literal laying on of hands, along with the visual geography of distinct pages.
ex.t: 拿着纸书时，你能实实在在地用手翻阅，还能看到一页页分明的视觉布局。

ex.s: People often link their memory of what they’ve read to how far into the book it was or where it was on the page.
ex.t: 人们常把对所读内容的记忆与它出现在书中的位置或页面上的位置联系起来。

ex.s: However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.
ex.t: 然而，心理学家已证明，成年人阅读新闻故事时，比听或看相同内容能记住更多内容。

ex.s: In the race to document the species on Earth before they go extinct, researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records.
ex.t: 在赶在物种灭绝前记录地球物种的竞赛中，研究人员和公民科学家已收集了数十亿条记录。

ex.s: Today, most records of biodiversity are often in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records.
ex.t: 如今，大多数生物多样性记录往往以照片、视频和其他数字记录的形式存在。

ex.s: Though they are useful for detecting shifts in the number and variety of species in an area, a new Stanford study has found that this type of record is not perfect.
ex.t: 尽管它们有助于探测一个地区物种数量和种类的变化，但斯坦福大学的一项新研究发现，这类记录并不完美。

ex.s: “With the rise of technology it is easy for people to make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application,” said Barnabas Daru, who is lead author of the study and assistant professor of biology in the Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences.
ex.t: 该研究的主要作者、斯坦福人文与科学学院生物学助理教授巴纳巴斯·达鲁说：“随着科技的发展，人们很容易借助手机应用观察不同的物种。”

ex.s: Using a global dataset of 1.9 billion records of plants, insects, birds, and animals, Daru and his team tested how well these data represent actual global biodiversity patterns.
ex.t: 达鲁和他的团队利用包含19亿条植物、昆虫、鸟类和动物记录的全球数据集，检验了这些数据对全球生物多样性真实模式的代表性如何。

ex.s: Their study revealed that the large number of observation-only records did not lead to better global coverage.
ex.t: 他们的研究表明，大量仅基于观察的记录并没有带来更好的全球覆盖。

ex.s: What can we do with the imperfect datasets of biodiversity?
ex.t: 面对这些不完美的生物多样性数据集，我们能做些什么？

ex.s: “Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled.
ex.t: “生物多样性应用可以利用我们的研究结果告知用户哪些地区采样过度，并引导他们去那些采样不足的地方——甚至去关注采样不足的物种。

ex.s: To improve the quality of observational data, biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image.”
ex.t: 为了提高观察数据的质量，生物多样性应用还可以鼓励用户请专家确认其上传图片的物种鉴定。”

ex.s: What do we know about the records of species collected now?
ex.t: 关于目前收集的物种记录，我们了解到什么？

ex.s: Poor quality of uploaded pictures.
ex.t: 上传图片质量差。

ex.s: Improper way of sampling.
ex.t: 采样方式不当。

ex.s: Confirm the identity of the users.
ex.t: 确认用户的身份。

ex.s: I don't trust my laptop's spellchecker. ____37____ Of course, these days there are plenty of online dictionaries and thesauruses, but I'm old-fashioned enough to prefer a hard cover and pages I can leaf through with my fingers.

ex.s: In addition, I have an old two-volume copy of the Shorter Oxford Dictionary, picked up a few years ago in a bookshop sale for just 99 pence.
ex.t: 此外，我还有一套旧的两卷本《简编牛津词典》，是几年前在书店促销时只花99便士淘到的。

ex.s: Of course, with its 2,672 pages, it's not exactly short.
ex.t: 当然，它有2672页，实在算不上“简编”。

ex.s: It contains around 163,000 words, plus word combinations and idiomatic phrases. ____39____ However, if I need to check the origin of a word or to look up examples of its usage, there's nothing better.
ex.t: 它收录了约16.3万个单词，外加词语搭配和惯用短语。____ 不过，如果我需要查一个单词的词源或查找其用法例句，没有比它更好的了。

ex.s: For well over a hundred years the most influential English dictionary was Samuel Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language published in 1755.
ex.t: 在长达一百多年的时间里，最有影响力的英语词典是塞缪尔·约翰逊1755年出版的《英语词典》。

ex.s: Of course, a dictionary is not only for spelling.

ex.s: On March 7, 1907, the English statistician Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the “wisdom of crowds” effect.
ex.t: 1907年3月7日，英国统计学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿发表了一篇论文，阐述了后来被称为“群体智慧”效应的现象。

ex.s: The experiment of estimation he conducted showed that in some cases, the average of a large number of independent estimates could be quite accurate.
ex.t: 他进行的估算实验表明，在某些情况下，大量独立估算的平均值可以相当准确。

ex.s: When enough of these errors are averaged together, they cancel each other out, resulting in a more accurate estimate.
ex.t: 当足够多的这类错误被平均在一起时，它们会相互抵消，从而得出更准确的估算。

ex.s: In more technical terms, the wisdom of crowds requires that people’s estimates be independent.
ex.t: 用更专业的术语来说，群体智慧要求人们的估算相互独立。

ex.s: If for whatever reasons, people’s errors become correlated or dependent, the accuracy of the estimate will go down.
ex.t: 如果由于某种原因，人们的错误变得相互关联或相互依赖，估算的准确性就会下降。

ex.s: The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals.
ex.t: 该研究的关键发现是：当人群被进一步分成可以进行讨论的小组时，这些小组的平均值比同等数量的独立个体的平均值更准确。

ex.s: For instance, the average obtained from the estimates of four discussion groups of five was significantly more accurate than the average obtained from 20 independent individuals.
ex.t: 例如，由四个五人讨论小组得出的平均估算值，明显比由20个独立个体得出的平均值更准确。

ex.s: In a follow-up study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group members actually did in their discussion.
ex.t: 在一项有100名大学生参加的后续研究中，研究人员试图更好地了解小组成员在讨论中实际做了什么。

ex.s: This happened some of the time, but it wasn’t the dominant response.

ex.s: Reading Art: Art for Book Lovers is a celebration of an everyday object — the book, represented here in almost three hundred artworks from museums around the world.
ex.t: 《阅读的艺术：爱书人的艺术》是对一种日常物品——书的礼赞，书中汇集了近三百件来自世界各地博物馆的艺术作品来呈现它。

ex.s: The image of the reader appears throughout history, in art made long before books as we now know them came into being.
ex.t: 读者的形象贯穿整个历史，出现在远早于我们今天所熟知的书籍诞生之前的艺术作品中。

ex.s: In artists’ representations of books and reading, we see moments of shared humanity that go beyond culture and time.
ex.t: 在艺术家对书籍和阅读的描绘中，我们看到了超越文化与时代的、人类共有的瞬间。

ex.s: In this “book of books,” artworks are selected and arranged in a way that emphasizes these connections between different eras and cultures.
ex.t: 在这本“书中的书”里，艺术作品的挑选和编排方式突出了不同时代和文化之间的这些联系。

ex.s: We see scenes of children learning to read at home or at school, with the book as a focus for relations between the generations.
ex.t: 我们看到孩子们在家中或学校学习阅读的场景，书本成为几代人之间关系的焦点。

ex.s: These scenes may have been painted hundreds of years ago, but they record moments we can all relate to.
ex.t: 这些场景也许是数百年前画下的，但它们记录了我们每个人都能感同身受的时刻。

ex.s: Before the wide use of the printing press, books were treasured objects and could be works of art in their own right.
ex.t: 在印刷术广泛使用之前，书籍是珍贵的物品，其本身就可以是艺术品。

ex.s: From a 21st-century point of view, the printed book is certainly ancient, but it remains as interactive as any battery-powered e-reader.
ex.t: 从21世纪的视角看，印刷书当然古老，但它与任何电池供电的电子阅读器一样具有互动性。

ex.s: And in contrast to our increasingly networked lives where the information we consume is monitored and tracked, a printed book still offers the chance of a wholly private, “off-line” activity.
ex.t: 而且，与我们日益网络化的生活——我们所消费的信息受到监控和追踪——形成对比的是，印刷书仍然提供了一种完全私密的、“离线”活动的机会。

ex.t: 一篇现代绘画评论。

ex.s: The printed book is not totally out of date.

ex.s: Past research has found health and wellness benefits of nature for humans, but a new study shows that wildness in urban areas is extremely important for human well-being.
ex.t: 过去的研究发现了大自然对人类健康和幸福的益处，而一项新研究表明，城市中的自然野趣对人类的幸福极其重要。

ex.s: They surveyed several hundred park-goers, asking them to submit a written summary online of a meaningful interaction they had with nature in the park.
ex.t: 他们调查了数百名游园者，请他们在线提交一份书面小结，描述他们在公园中与自然进行的一次有意义的互动。

ex.s: For example, one participant’s experience of “We sat and listened to the waves at the beach for a while” was assigned the categories “sitting at beach” and “listening to waves.”
ex.t: 例如，一位参与者的经历“我们在海滩上坐着听了一会儿海浪”被归入“坐在海滩上”和“听海浪”两个类别。

ex.s: Across the 320 submissions, a pattern of categories the researchers call a “nature language” began to emerge.
ex.t: 在320份提交材料中，一种被研究人员称为“自然语言”的类别模式开始显现。

ex.s: After the coding of all submissions, half a dozen categories were noted most often as important to visitors.
ex.t: 对所有提交材料进行编码后，有六种类别最常被游客提及为重要。

ex.s: These include encountering wildlife, walking along the edge of water, and following an established trail.
ex.t: 这些类别包括遇见野生动物、沿着水边散步，以及沿着既有的小径行走。

ex.s: For example, the experience of walking along the edge of water might be satisfying for a young professional on a weekend hike in the park.
ex.t: 例如，沿着水边散步的体验，对一位周末在公园里徒步的年轻职场人士来说可能很令人满足。

ex.s: Back downtown during a workday, they can enjoy a more domestic form of this interaction by walking along a fountain on their lunch break.
ex.t: 回到市中心的上班日，他们可以在午休时间沿着喷泉散步，享受这种互动的一种更居家化的形式。

ex.s: And for that to happen, we also need to protect nature so that we can interact with it,” said Peter Kahn, a senior author of the study.
ex.t: 要做到这一点，我们还需要保护自然，这样我们才能与它互动，”该研究的资深作者彼得·卡恩说。

ex.t: 最近有报道称，坚持传统饮食的人数正在缓慢下降，大约一半的英国消费者希望以某种方式改变或改进自己的烹饪。

ex.s: Ideally a history would bring together texts and objects, and some chapters of this book are able to do just that, but in many cases we simply can’t.
ex.t: 理想情况下，一部历史应该把文字和实物结合起来，本书的某些章节能够做到这一点，但在许多情况下我们根本做不到。

ex.s: The clearest example of this between literate and non-literate history is perhaps the first conflict, at Botany Bay, between Captain Cook’s voyage and the Australian Aboriginals.
ex.t: 在有文字和无文字历史之间，最清楚的例子也许是库克船长的航行与澳大利亚原住民在植物湾发生的第一次冲突。

ex.s: From the English side, we have scientific reports and the captain’s record of that terrible day.
ex.t: 从英方那里，我们有科学报告和船长对那可怕一天的记录。

ex.s: From the Australian side, we have only a wooden shield (盾) dropped by a man in flight after his first experience of gunshot.
ex.t: 从澳大利亚一方那里，我们只有一面木盾（盾），是一个人在第一次经历枪击后逃跑时丢下的。

ex.s: In addition to the problem of miscomprehension from both sides, there are victories accidentally or deliberately twisted, especially when only the victors know how to write.
ex.t: 除了双方相互误解的问题之外，还有一些胜利被无意或有意地歪曲，尤其是当只有胜利者懂得书写的时候。

ex.s: The Caribbean Taino, the Australian Aboriginals, the African people of Benin and the Incas, all of whom appear in this book, can speak to us now of their past achievements most powerfully through the objects they made: a history told through things gives them back a voice.
ex.t: 加勒比海的泰诺人、澳大利亚原住民、贝宁的非洲人和印加人——他们都出现在本书中——如今可以通过他们制作的物品最有力地向我们讲述他们过去的成就：一部通过实物讲述的历史把声音还给了他们。

ex.s: If we are to find the other half of that conversation, we have to read not just the texts, but the objects.
ex.t: 如果我们要找到那场对话的另一半，我们就不仅要读文字，还要读实物。

ex.s: And unlike what we suppose, storytelling is not just a form of entertainment, but a form of learning as well.

ex.s: The inability to engage with longer-term causes and consequences leads to some of the world’s most serious problems: climate change, biodiversity collapse, and more.
ex.t: 无法关注长期的原因和后果导致了一些世界上最严重的问题：气候变化、生物多样性丧失等等。

ex.s: The historian Francis Cole argues that the West has entered a period where “only the present exists, a present characterised at once by the cruelty of the instant and by the boredom of an unending now”.
ex.t: 历史学家弗朗西斯·科尔认为，西方已进入一个"只有当下存在的时期，这个当下的特征是瞬间的残酷和无尽现在的无聊并存"。

ex.s: One of them is about how the most accessible information in the present affects decisions about the future.
ex.t: 其中之一是关于当前最容易获取的信息如何影响对未来做出的决策。

ex.s: Indeed, when it comes to environmental transformations, we can develop a form of collective “poor memory”, and each new generation can believe the state of affairs they encounter is nothing out of the ordinary.
ex.t: 事实上，在环境变化方面，我们可以形成一种集体的"糟糕记忆"，每一代新人都可以认为他们遇到的状况没有什么不寻常的。

ex.s: Lessons of history are highly valued.
ex.t: 历史的教训受到高度重视。

ex.s: The reason is simple: we know of just one type of life and it’s challenging to do science with a sample size of one.
ex.t: 原因很简单：我们只知道一种生命形式，而仅凭一个样本做科学是很有挑战性的。

ex.s: The field of artificial life-called ALife for short — is the systematic attempt to spell out life’s fundamental principles.
ex.t: 人工生命领域——简称ALife——是系统性地阐明生命基本原理的尝试。

ex.s: Many of these practitioners, so-called ALifers, think that somehow making life is the surest way to really understand what life is.
ex.t: 这些从业者中的许多——所谓的ALife研究者——认为，以某种方式创造生命是真正理解生命的最佳途径。

ex.s: This track record makes ALife a ripe target for criticism, such as declarations of the field’s doubtful scientific value.
ex.t: 这使得ALife成为批评的有力目标，例如对该领域科学价值的质疑。

ex.s: Alan Smith, a complexity scientist, is tired of such complaints.
ex.t: 艾伦·史密斯是一位复杂性科学家，他已经厌倦了这种抱怨。

ex.s: Asking about “the point” of ALife might be, well, missing the point entirely, he says.
ex.t: 询问ALife的"意义"可能——嗯——完全偏离了重点，他说。

ex.s: “Some people ask me, ‘So what’s the worth of artificial life?’ Do you ever think, ‘What is the worth of your grandmother?’”
ex.t: "有人问我，'那人工生命有什么价值？'你有没有想过，'你祖母的价值是什么？'"

ex.s: This is the capacity for a system to create essentially endless complexity, to be a sort of “novelty generator”.
ex.t: 这是一个系统创造本质上无限复杂性的能力，成为一种"新颖性生成器"。

ex.s: If the field of ALife manages to reproduce life’s endless “creativity” in some virtual model, those same principles could give rise to truly inventive machines.
ex.t: 如果ALife领域能够在某些虚拟模型中复制生命无限的"创造力"，那么同样的原理可能会催生真正具有创造力的机器。

ex.s: Compared with the developments of Al, advances in ALife are harder to recognize.
ex.t: 与人工智能的发展相比，ALife的进展更难被识别。

ex.s: The lack of agreement among ALifers doesn’t help either.
ex.t: ALife研究者之间的缺乏共识也无济于事。

ex.s: The result is a diverse line of projects that each advance along their unique paths.
ex.t: 结果是形成了多样化的项目系列，每个项目都沿着各自独特的路径前进。

ex.s: It may be, of course, that these characteristics aren’t in any way surprising or singular.
ex.t: 当然，这些特征可能在任何方面都不令人惊讶或独特。

ex.s: They may apply universally to all acts of evolution.
ex.t: 它们可能普遍适用于所有进化行为。

ex.s: But even this dismissal suggests something：perhaps, just like life itself throughout the universe, the rise of ALife will prove unavoidable.
ex.t: 但即使是这种否定也暗示着某种东西：也许就像宇宙中的生命本身一样，ALife的兴起将是不可避免的。

ex.s: Human speech contains more than 2,000 different sounds, from the common “m” and “a” to the rare clicks of some southern African languages.
ex.t: 人类语音包含2000多种不同的声音，从常见的"m"和"a"到某些南部非洲语言中罕见的咔嗒声。

ex.s: More than 30 years ago, the scholar Charles Hockett noted that speech sounds called labiodentals, such as “f” and “v”, were more common in the languages of societies that ate softer foods.
ex.t: 30多年前，学者Charles Hockett注意到，被称为唇齿音的语音（如"f"和"v"）在饮食较软的社会的语言中更为常见。

ex.s: Now a team of researchers led by Damián Blasi at the University of Zurich, Switzerland, has found how and why this trend arose.
ex.t: 现在，由苏黎世大学的Damián Blasi领导的研究团队发现了这种趋势是如何以及为何产生的。

ex.s: The team showed that this change in bite was connected with the development of agriculture in the Neolithic period.
ex.t: 团队表明，这种咬合变化与新石器时代农业的发展有关。

ex.s: Analyses of a language database also confirmed that there was a global change in the sound of world languages after the Neolithic age, with the use of “f” and “v” increasing remarkably during the last few thousand years.
ex.t: 对语言数据库的分析也证实，新石器时代之后世界语言的声音发生了全球性变化，"f"和"v"的使用在过去几千年中显著增加。

ex.s: These sounds are still not found in the languages of many hunter-gatherer people today.
ex.t: 这些声音在今天许多狩猎采集民族的语言中仍然不存在。

ex.s: This research overturns the popular view that all human speech sounds were present when human beings evolved around 300,000 years ago. ”The set of speech sounds we use has not necessarily remained stable since the appearance of human beings, but rather the huge variety of speech sounds that we find today is the product of a complex interplay of things like biological change and cultural evolution,“ said Steven Moran, a member of the research team.
ex.t: 这项研究推翻了人类在大约30万年前进化时所有语音就已经存在的流行观点。"我们使用的语音集合自人类出现以来不一定保持稳定，相反，我们今天发现的巨大语音多样性是生物变化和文化进化等复杂相互作用的结果，"研究团队成员Steven Moran说。

ex.s: Recently，I conceptualized a new approach to timekeeping that's connected to circumstances on our planet，conditions that might change as a result of global warming．We're now building a clock at the Anchorage Museum that reflects the total flow of several major Alaskan rivers，which are sensitive to local and global environmental changes．We've programmed it to match an atomic clock if the waterways continue to flow at their present rate．If the rivers run faster in the future on average，the clock will get ahead of standard time．If they run slower，you'll see the opposite effect．
ex.t: 最近我构想了一种与地球环境状况相关联的新型计时方式这些状况可能因全球变暖而发生变化．我们正在安克雷奇博物馆建造一座钟它反映了几条主要阿拉斯加河流的总流量这些河流对当地和全球的环境变化都很敏感．我们已经编程让它在水流保持当前速率时与原子钟同步．如果将来河流平均流速加快钟会比标准时间走得快．如果河流变慢你会看到相反的效果．

ex.s: Even if this method of timekeeping is novel in its particulars，early agricultural societies also connected time to natural phenomena．In pre-Classical Greece，for instance，people“corrected”official calendars by shifting dates forward or backward to reflect the change of season．Temporal connection to the environment was vital to their survival．Likewise，river time and other timekeeping systems we're developing may encourage environmental awareness．
ex.t: 即使这种计时方法的具体细节是新颖的早期农业社会也将时间与自然现象联系起来．例如在前古典希腊时期人们通过向前或向后调整日期来"修正"官方历法以反映季节的变化．与环境的时间联系对他们的生存至关重要．同样河流时间和其他我们正在开发的计时系统可能会促进环保意识．

ex.s: When St．Augustine admitted his inability to define time， he highlighted one of time 's most noticeable qualities：Time becomes meaningful only in a defined context．Any timekeeping system is valid，and each is as praiseworthy as its purpose．
ex.t: 当圣奥古斯丁承认他无法定义时间时他突出了时间最显著的特征之一：时间只有在特定的语境下才有意义．任何计时系统都是有效的每种都因其目的而值得称赞．

ex.s: If you see humor as an optional form of entertainment, you’re missing some of its biggest benefits: Humor makes average-looking people look cute and uninteresting people seem entertaining.

ex.s: Best of all, humor raises your energy, and that can have an effect on everything you do at school, at work, or in your personal life.

ex.s: I always wanted to know what my mom was reading． Hearing mom say，"I can't believe what's printed in the newspaper this morning，" made me want to grab it out of her hands and read it myself． I wanted to be like my mom and know all of the things she knew． So I carried around a book， and each night， just to be like her， I would pretend to be reading．

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．

ex.s: Most of my reading through primary， middle and high school was factual reading． I read for knowledge， and to make A's on my tests． Occasionally， I would read a novel that was assigned， but I didn't enjoy this type of reading． I liked facts， things that are concrete． I thought anything abstract left too much room for argument．
